properties.name: WHAT WORKED (hxm_program, 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-28): revising a finding and a decision kept what each used to say, and it mattered both times. One mapping recorded as "confirmed" was corrected twice in a day, and one decision was reversed three hours after it was made
properties.statement:
Recorded so a regression is checkable. Two sightings from the hxm_program hub.
· 2026-09-25 (reflow2 0.69.0 → 0.70.0): "`record_finding` revisions kept prior text in snapshots, which mattered: a camera mapping recorded as 'confirmed' was wrong by physical position and had to be corrected twice in one day."
· 2026-09-28 (0.73.0): "Revising a decision preserved what it used to say. [A pull request]'s scope was reversed three hours after it was decided ('device-only' became 'also the plan fixes CI needed'). `add_decision` on the same id replaced the text and reported `prior_state_preserved_in: snap:epoch:preserved-on-write:…`. The history is right, and nobody had to remember to snapshot."
What must not regress:
· a revise through the ordinary constructor keeps the replaced value when nothing else holds it;
· the reply names where it went (cap:a-revising-write-says-whether-the-state-survived).
The same week's report counts the cost beside it: the reversal was also re-written by hand in two file-side copies (F-34, triaged separately).
